risk.title: Failure to notify borrower promptly of a missed payment and unpaid sums under CONC 7.20.1R(2)(a)
risk.description:
The firm may not notify the borrower, as soon as possible after a missed payment, that the payment has occurred and of any sums that have become payable but remain unpaid (including unpaid charges for non-compliance). Risk drivers include missed payment detection, timing of notification, and the accuracy of unpaid sums data. Because the rule fixes no number of days, the timing standard needs expert confirmation. This proposal overlaps with an existing approved catalogue risk, which is mapped below.

Inherent rating: HIGH (provisional) — CONC 7.20.1R(2)(a) is a binding rule requiring the firm to notify the borrower as soon as possible after a missed payment of the missed payment and of any unpaid sums, including unpaid charges. If this is missed, borrowers may not know they are in arrears, may incur further charges or adverse credit consequences, and the firm may breach a binding FCA rule that takes effect on 15 July 2026. The rating is drawn from the verified quotation in REG-1 and the impact summary in IMP-1; it is an inherent rating only and requires human validation.
Residual rating: UNASSESSED — no control-effectiveness evidence is available.

Requires human confirmation — not verified organisational fact.

riskProposals.title: Insufficient or incomplete information on missed payment consequences under CONC 7.20.1R(2)(b)
riskProposals.description: The firm may fail to give the borrower sufficient information to understand which agreement the missed payment relates to, the adverse consequences arising or likely to arise, and, where relevant, the steps available to mitigate them. Risk drivers include undefined thresholds for 'adverse consequences', 'sufficient information' and 'relevant' mitigation, inconsistent judgement across cases, and weak evidence of the firm's assessment of likely consequences. Expert judgement is needed on each of these.
riskProposals.inherent_rationale: CONC 7.20.1R(2)(b) is a standalone binding obligation requiring the firm to provide sufficient information for the borrower to understand the agreement concerned, adverse consequences (actual and likely) and relevant mitigation steps. If it is missed, borrowers may not understand the consequences of arrears or how to mitigate them, which risks consumer harm and a rule breach. The rule sets an outcome standard rather than a content list, which raises the risk of inconsistent application; the evidence comes from REG-1.

riskProposals.title: Failure to provide required missed payment information together under CONC 7.20.1R(3)
riskProposals.description: The notification and information required under CONC 7.20.1R(2) may be issued separately, in fragments or through different channels or at different times, rather than together. This could arise from separate systems or teams producing the notification and the consequence and mitigation information.
riskProposals.inherent_rationale: CONC 7.20.1R(3) is a standalone binding requirement that the information required under CONC 7.20.1R(2) must be provided together. If it is missed, borrowers may receive partial or disjointed communications, which weakens their understanding of the missed payment and its consequences and breaches the rule. The rating is MEDIUM because the obligation is narrower in scope than the notification and content duties, based on the limb text in REG-1; it requires human validation.

limbs.text: This rule applies where a borrower has failed to make a payment by the time it has fallen due under the terms of a regulated deferred payment credit agreement (‘a missed payment’).
As soon as possible after a missed payment has occurred the firm must:
notify the borrower:
that the missed payment has occurred; and
about any sums which have become payable under the regulated deferred payment credit agreement but remain unpaid (including unpaid charges for non-compliance with the agreement); and
provide the borrower with sufficient information for the borrower to understand:
which regulated deferred payment credit agreement the missed payment relates to;
any adverse consequences for the borrower arising out of the missed payment;
any adverse consequences for the borrower that the firm considers are likely to arise out of the missed payment; and
(where relevant) any steps the borrower can take to mitigate those adverse consequences.
The information required under (2) must be provided together.
In this rule references to ‘payment’ refer to the repayment of capital but exclude payment of a charge for non-compliance with a regulated deferred payment credit agreement.

provisionBreakdown.verbatim: 7.20.1 R (1) This rule applies where a borrower has failed to make a payment by the time it has fallen due under the terms of a regulated deferred payment credit agreement (‘a missed payment’). (2) As soon as possible after a missed payment has occurred the firm must: (a) notify the borrower: (i) that the missed payment has occurred; and (ii) about any sums which have become payable under the regulated deferred payment credit agreement but remain unpaid (including unpaid charges for non-compliance with the agreement); and (b) provide the borrower with sufficient information for the borrower to understand: (i) which regulated deferred payment credit agreement the missed payment relates to; (ii) any adverse consequences for the borrower arising out of the missed payment; (iii) any adverse consequences for the borrower that the firm considers are likely to arise out of the missed payment; and (iv) (where relevant) any steps the borrower can take to mitigate those adverse consequences. (3) The information required under (2) must be provided together. (4) In this rule references to ‘payment’ refer to the repayment of capital but exclude payment of a charge for non-compliance with a regulated deferred payment credit agreement.
